title: 14 New Things Your iPhone Can Do in iOS 27.2
content:
Apple released iOS 27.2 on October 26, bringing enhancements to Siri AI, adding Suggestions in Messages, and sneaking in a string of smaller additions across Photos, Podcasts, Games, Apple TV, and FaceTime. 


iOS 27.2 is available to download to your device now via Settings ➝ General ➝ Software Update. Note that some features may not be available in all regions or on all iPhone models. Apple maintains a feature availability list with all the details.

Ask Siri About Past Conversations


Siri AI can now recall your past conversations, so you can ask it about something it told you before, like the restaurants it recommended last week. Siri AI features require an iPhone 16 model or later, or an iPhone 15 Pro or iPhone 15 Pro Max.

Get Answers From More of Your Personal Context


Siri AI can now draw from more sources when answering, including photos attached in Messages, Calendar event attendees, and your voicemails. Apple says you'll also get better results from Safari history and Reading List.

Use Siri in More Languages


Siri AI now supports French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish, in addition to English. Just keep in mind that, as things stand, it's not available in the EU or mainland China.

Control Which Apps Siri and Search Can Access


A new settings menu has been added that lets you choose which apps Siri, Search, and suggestions can access, all from one list. You can find it in Settings ➝ Siri ➝ Excluded Apps.

Copy Just Part of a Siri Response


Granular text selection lets you select and copy only the part of a Siri response you need, rather than the whole reply.

Act on Suggestions in Messages


held back from the initial release, so its arrival has been a good while coming.

Manage Shared Albums More Easily


Shared Albums in Photos gain three additions. You can now edit captions and comments, the app can avoid adding duplicate photos, and it can display a reminder before an album expires so participants can save important photos and videos.

Spot AI-Generated Images


iOS 27.2 supports SynthID watermarking, which aims to help you identify whether an image was generated or modified with generative tools in Photos and Image Playground.

See What Your Friends Are Playing


In the Games app, the Friends tab now provides context around friend suggestions, plus it shows you any recent games your friends have played on their player pages.

Create Apple TV Profiles for Your Household


If you have an Apple TV, you can now create profiles in the account settings section on iPhone and iPad. All you need for a profile is a name, plus whether it's for an adult or a child. Creating a profile for a child limits content to a PG rating by default, but there's a customize option for finer control. You can select age ratings for TV shows and movies that are appropriate for the child based on their age.

Stream FaceTime From Front and Rear Cameras


Dual Capture is now available in group ‌FaceTime‌ calls, so you can stream ‌FaceTime‌ video content from the front and rear cameras at the same time. On a compatible device running ‌iOS 27‌.2, flipping the camera while on a ‌FaceTime‌ call automatically turns on Dual Capture.

Dual Capture is available on the iPhone 17, ‌iPhone 17‌ Pro, ‌iPhone 17‌ Pro Max, iPhone Air, iPhone 18 Pro, ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max, and ‌iPhone Duo‌.

Watch Several Live Sports Streams at Once


Multiview has been expanded in the Apple TV app to the iPhone, so you can now watch up to four live sports streams at the same time. Multiview works for sports events that come with an ‌Apple TV‌ subscription, so that's Major League Soccer (MLS), Formula 1 (F1) in the U.S., and Friday Night Baseball doubleheaders during the Major League Baseball season.

iPhone Duo Edge Light and Apple Pencil Support
 

iOS 27.2 adds Apple Pencil USB-C support to the ‌iPhone Duo‌. It also includes support for the Edge Light feature that first appeared in macOS to illuminate your face during video calls.

Be Reminded of a Contact's Anniversary on a Call

title: iPhone Duo Review: One Week Later
content:
It's been a week since the iPhone Duo was released, and MacRumors videographer Dan Barbera wanted to revisit his review since he's been able to use the Duo for a longer stretch of time.

Subscribe to the MacRumors YouTube channel for more videos.

You've probably seen images of iPhone Duos with a bright white line running across one side of the inner display. There is a defect affecting some users, but Apple says it's a problem limited to a small number of units.

MacRumors have had a display crack, and we've seen some AI photos floating around, so it's hard to tell just how many people are actually having problems. iPhone Duos with the hinge issue that causes the display to crack seem to get damaged shortly after purchase, so if you've had an ‌iPhone Duo‌ for the last week and it's still fine, it's not likely to have this defect.

The outer display is small, but Dan finds it useful for checking notifications, replying to messages, and scrolling through apps and websites. He unfolds it for multitasking or longer messages, and is a fan of using the ‌iPhone Duo‌ unfolded in portrait mode for watching videos and using an app at the same time.

Touch ID fingerprint sensor easy to find, and says Apple Watch unlock is similar to Face ID. The cameras are just okay, and someone who zooms in a lot is probably going to miss having a telephoto lens.

iPhone 18 Pro and a Pro Max, and for most people, it's likely going to last a full day. Not all apps have been updated for the Duo layout yet, but it's getting better. There's an extension called Wider that extends the Safari window to the edges of the ‌iPhone Duo‌'s outer display, and it's a big improvement. We may see other accommodations in the coming months as developers and users get used to the new layout.

Dan says the ‌iPhone Duo‌ is the most excited he's been about an iPhone in a long time, and he plans to keep using it even though he misses having a telephoto lens.

title: MacBook Pro With Touch Display: 15 More Details Revealed
content:
Apple on Wednesday unveiled new 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro models with touch-enabled OLED displays, and more details about them continue to be shared by tech reporters who were invited to Apple's hands-on experience in Los Angeles.


Nicolas Lellouche of the French website Numerama shared 15 details about the new MacBook Pro models in an article and a social media post. Some of this information has already surfaced, but he provided a useful summary:

Apple said the keyboard and trackpad remain the primary input methods, with touch input available as an additional option for those who want it.

Apple said there is now a generation of young creators who grew up using touchscreens, so it felt the timing was right to bring the functionality to the Mac.

Apple said music creators prefer touch over trackpads for controlling virtual instruments.

"Traffic light" controls in the top-left corner of macOS windows expand when pressed.

Items in a list become more spaced out when touched.

A swipe up from the bottom of the screen brings up the Dock.

A swipe down from the top of the screen brings up Spotlight/Siri AI.

A long press is equivalent to a right click.

Holding a window and quickly moving it left or right triggers Split View.

If you close your Mac while your finger is touching the display, touch input is temporarily deactivated to prevent accidental touches.

The camera is stabilized so it does not shake on video calls when you touch the screen.

You cannot wake the MacBook Pro by touching the screen.

Multi-touch supports up to 10 fingers at the same time. No word yet on toes (kidding).

Live Activities from iPhone apps can appear in the Dynamic Island.

There are settings that allow you to turn off touch input and the illuminated Apple logo on the MacBook Pro's lid.

title: The MacRumors Show: OLED MacBook Pro, iPad Mini 8, and More
content:
On this week's episode of The MacRumors Show, we discuss Apple's newly announced OLED MacBook Pro, iPad mini with A20 Pro, and M6 versions of the iMac and entry-level 14-inch ‌MacBook Pro‌.

Subscribe to The MacRumors Show YouTube channel for more videos

The MacBook Pro gains a tandem ‌OLED‌ display with touch support for the first time. Available in 14- and 16-inch sizes, the "PROLED XDR display" offers up to 2,000 nits of peak HDR and SDR brightness, a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio, and Adobe RGB support alongside P3. Touch input enables gestures such as scrolling, pinching to zoom, and dragging content, with a reinforced hinge and camera stabilization designed to accommodate interaction with the screen.

Dynamic Island replaces the notch, providing access to Live Activities, Siri AI, and more. The enclosure is thinner and lighter, with the 14-inch model weighing 3 pounds and the 16-inch model weighing 4 pounds. The larger model's display grows to 16.3 inches, and the iconic illuminated Apple logo returns.

upgraded speakers with 50% deeper bass and dedicated tuning for closed-lid playback. Maximum storage doubles to 16TB. Pricing starts at $2,899 for the 14-inch model and $3,399 for the 16-inch model, a $400 premium over comparable mini-LED configurations.

nano-texture option on the 256GB and 512GB configurations. It is thinner and lighter at 5.4mm thick, and becomes the first iPad with an official IP67 water and dust resistance rating. The display remains limited to 60Hz, with no ProMotion support.

additional CPU core and a second 16-core Neural Engine compared with the 128GB and 256GB models.

Acoustic Display speaker system eliminates external speaker holes, while the front camera moves to the landscape edge and the rear camera gains an Adaptive True Tone flash. Other additions include fast charging, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, Thread, Apple's C2 modem on cellular models, and extended external display support with iPadOS 27.2. The ‌iPad mini‌ starts at $699 in Midnight or Starlight, with a new $79 TechWoven Smart Folio available separately.

M6 iMac replaces the M4 model, adding two CPU and GPU cores to both the two-port and four-port configurations. It also gains GPU Neural Accelerators, dual 16-core Neural Engines, up to twice as fast SSD storage, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, Thread, and 2.5 Gigabit Ethernet. Pricing starts at $1,499, with the four-port model starting at $1,699.

14-inch MacBook Pro moves from M5 to M6, with a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU, dual 16-core Neural Engines, and upgraded wireless connectivity. Memory bandwidth increases to 170GB/s on 24GB and 32GB configurations, while the 16GB model remains at 153GB/s. Its $1,999 starting price and battery life of up to 24 hours carry over from the outgoing model.

title: How to turn a Siri Remote into a handy Mac controller
content:
A Siri Remote can make controlling a Mac from across the room much easier, and with one utility you can use it as a small trackpad, although you'll need more than macOS's built-in support to get the full experience.

Siri Remote with Mac
If your Mac mini is connected to a TV, or you use your MacBook for presentations, reaching for a keyboard to control playback isn't always convenient. An Apple TV Siri Remote lets you manage basic controls from across the room without returning to your Mac.
A Siri Remote connects to a Mac over Bluetooth, and macOS already supports some of its buttons. However, Apple designed the remote for Apple TV, so its clickpad doesn't automatically control the mouse or navigate Mac apps.
Basic controls work without additional software, while third-party apps add more functionality. Whether it's worth setting up depends on how much control you need and whether you're willing to switch the remote between your Mac and Apple TV.

title: Russia Places Apple on State Surveillance Registry
content:
Apple faces Russian data retention and disclosure requirements after being added to the country's state surveillance registry, Bloomberg reports.


Russia's communications regulator, Roskomnadzor, listed Apple and Microsoft on October 2 as "organizers of information dissemination," a classification that carries obligations to preserve communications and make data available to Russian security agencies.

Those obligations cover correspondence and messages containing audio or video. Companies must also keep information identifying users and recording the transmission of their communications within Russia for three years. Businesses that fail to meet the requirements risk fines and, ultimately, restrictions on their services.

Apple and Microsoft join other services on the registry, including WhatsApp, Telegram, and Snapchat. Google and its Meet video calling service were listed in January.

December 2025 block on FaceTime. Roskomnadzor justified that restriction by alleging the service was being used to facilitate terrorism, recruitment, and fraud. Russia had already restricted calling through WhatsApp and Telegram and blocked Signal and Viber.

Two-tone pink, green, and blue color options, along with white and midnight.

3% weight reduction. Huge.

title: Rian Johnson's iPhone Camera App Goes Viral
content:
Filmmaker Rian Johnson, best known for writing and directing "Knives Out," "Glass Onion," and "Star Wars: The Last Jedi," has seen his new iPhone photography app Chromagraph Camera climb to the top of the paid App Store charts after attracting attention on social media this week.


Johnson developed the app with his longtime cinematographer Steve Yedlin and programmer Eric Cameron, bringing image processing techniques from their films to iPhone still photography. Chromagraph currently ranks No. 1 in Photo & Video on the U.S. App Store.

Johnson's announcement on X accumulated six million views within a day, while users have been sharing their results, with some photo posts attracting thousands of likes.





Chromagraph shoots RAW photos and processes them using techniques Yedlin developed for his films, giving pictures a distinctive treatment of color, contrast, and grain. It also adds halation, a soft glow around bright areas. Users can adjust the look with controls for color, tone, and texture.

The effect appears after taking a photo, when users open the app's gallery. Original RAW files are kept intact, so edits can be changed later.

For sharing, photographs can be exported as JPEG or HEIC files with the processing applied. An automatic export option also sends each finished photo to the user's photo library.

App Store and requires iOS 17 or later.

title: Got a Mac Pro collecting dust? This kit will convert it into a Windows PC
content:
Macworld





If you have an old “cheese-grater” Mac Pro, you probably don’t want to part with it. You look at it and wonder what you’re going to do with it, since it can’t be upgraded. Seems like a waste to throw it out, and you won’t get nearly enough to make it worth selling. Well, a Canadian mechatronics enthusiast understands your predicament and has set out to do something about it.
Stefan Bond has launched the Mac Pro 7,1 (A1991) ATX Conversion Kit project on Kickstarter. The kit can be used to install “modern PC hardware” into the chassis of a Mac Pro–specifically, the Mac Pro that was introduced in 2019 and identified with the model number 7,1. Since it was built with Mac hardware in mind, you can’t simply gut it and pop in a PC motherboard, a gigantic graphics card, and other components. The Conversion Kit will allow you to do that by providing a main motherboard and PSU mounting plate, hard drive sled assemblies and cables, Mac Pro fan-adapter PCBs, and more.
To be clear, this is a kit that enables you to install PC components (which aren’t included) for building a PC that runs Windows. There’s no official way to upgrade the Mac Pro with Apple components. If you really want to run macOS, you should be able to turn this into a Hackintosh after building it.
Bond has a goal of $10,000 for his Kickstarter, and a bid of $699 in Canadian currency (about $500 in the U.S.) gets you a full conversion kit. If you don’t have a Mac Pro but just want to contribute to the spirit of the project, you can chip in CA$10, and your name will be mentioned in the final project video.
Apple discontinued the Mac Pro earlier this year, ending a 20-year run for the Mac Pro brand. The latest time it was updated was in 2023, when Apple released it with an M2 Ultra chip. When this design was introduced in 2019, it had Intel processors. Apple offers the Mac Studio as its top Mac workstation, but it doesn’t have anywhere near the character of its old metal towers.

title: Touch isn’t the killer feature of the new MacBook Pro
content:
Macworld





Apple has finally brought a touch interface to the Mac, 43 years after the first commercial PC with a touchscreen, the HP 150. It’s a momentous event in Apple history, one that longtime Mac users never thought would come.
The new laptop is going to be mainly referred to as the “touchscreen MacBook Pro,” and there’s a lot of talk about the feature. But if you think of the new laptop only in terms of Touch, you’re missing the point. There’s a reason why Apple calls it the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display. It’s clumsy and lengthy, but notice how “Touch” isn’t one of the words.
“Touch” isn’t in the name because it’s not the most important new feature of the new MacBook Pro. In fact, Apple has a link to a white paper about the PROLED Display on the product wesbite, and Touch isn’t mentioned at all. I think it’s the least important feature, and there are other aspects of the laptop that are more important and have implications for other MacBooks down the line.
OLED takes the lead
The display is the most important feature, but not because of touch, but because it’s a tandem OLED display that can “deliver the kind of visual fidelity pros have been dreaming of,” according to Apple. Considering Apple’s long history of producing the best quality laptop displays, I’m inclined to believe that statement.

				
					

				
			
Apple




Look at these specs. This is on a laptop? Damn.
10,000,000:1 contrast ratio
XDR brightness: Up to 1000 nits sustained full-screen; 2000 nits peak (HDR content only)
SDR brightness: Up to 1000 nits sustained full-screen; 2000 nits peak (outdoor)
ProMotion adaptive refresh rates
1.00 percent reflectance, lower than traditional OLED displays
P3 + Adobe RGB wide color gamuts
Apple Color-Matching Functions 2026
Medical imaging support





That’s easily one of the best, if not the best display ever put in a laptop. Can a display on a laptop be so good-looking that you’ll never want to take your eyes off it? If it can, count on Apple to make it. 
What’s even more exciting is what it means for the rest of the MacBook lineup in the future. Several reports have said OLED is coming to the MacBook Air, possibly in 2028, and though it probably won’t be on the same level as the MacBook Pro with PROLED Display—consider the difference between the iPad mini and the iPad Pro—it’ll still be a major upgrade from the current LED-backlit IPS panel.
Lighter design
A few days ago, I was in the office with my 16-inch MacBook Pro in my backpack. I put my backpack on my desk, and it landed with a loud thud. My co-worker (a PC fanboy) was shocked. “What’s with the rocks in your bag?” he exclaimed
The new MacBook Pro is nearly a pound lighter. That might not sound like much, but it makes a difference if you’re moving around often, or if you’re like me and you have an hour-long commute on public transportation. Hopefully, that thud won’t be as resonant with the new laptop.
It’ll be interesting to see if the advances Apple made to achieve the smaller and lighter MacBook Pro will carry over to the other MacBooks. Imagine if the MacBook Neo and the 13-inch MacBook Air, Apple’s lightest laptops at 2.7 pounds, were closer to 2 pounds. 
Dynamic Island
The notch on the MacBooks is there because the bezel is too thin to fit the FaceTime camera, but it’s also just sort of… there. It’s not really obtrusive, because it sits above the usable screen space in the status bar, but it still feels like a vestigial part of the laptop with no real purpose.

				
					

				
			
Apple




The Dynamic Island replaces the notch, and it’s now a functional anchor of the Mac. It works as it does on the iPhone, so you know it’ll be a useful home for Spotlight search and Lite Activities. I’ve come to appreciate how it’s used on the iPhone, so I’m excited to see it become a natural extension of macOS.
Will the Dynamic Island make it to other MacBooks? It would be a shame if Apple decided it was a premium feature for only the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display, but I can see that happening. Apple won’t switch from the notch to the Dynamic Island until the other MacBooks upgrade their display tech, so we won’t know for some time.
Glowing Apple logo
It’s just a logo, but as Mac users and Apple fans, that Apple logo has meaning. When the glowing Apple was introduced in the 1999 PowerBook G3, it made a statement (even though it was upside down for the first couple of years). It told people we were proud Mac users. We mourned the loss of the logo in 2015.
But the glowing logo and the statement it brings are back. But this time it comes as a flex, the way that Cosmic Orange was for the iPhone 17 Pro. People who know Macs will see it and know you’ve got the new MacBook Pro. As for the people who don’t know Macs, well, they’ll see it and be envious. Best of all, the glowing Apple icon won’t be upside down when the lid is open. And now that it’s a little screen of its own, you can even turn it off if you want.

title: Apple's Touchscreen MacBook Pro Could Ship 1.5M Units in 2027
content:
Apple's new OLED touchscreen MacBook Pro could ship between 1.2 million and 1.5 million units in 2027, according to a new forecast from market intelligence firm TrendForce.


Announced on Wednesday, the new MacBook Pro is the first to feature a tandem OLED touchscreen, with pricing starting at $2,899 for the 14-inch model and $3,399 for the 16-inch model. Pre-orders are available now, with a launch coming on Friday, November 6. 

Given that Apple is selling the OLED models alongside its existing mini-LED MacBook Pro lineup, TrendForce says that the premium starting price could temper near-term replacement demand.

Even so, the firm expects Apple's arrival in the OLED laptop market to accelerate the market landscape more broadly. Up until now, it has been driven mainly by Windows brands such as Lenovo, HP, and ASUS. 

The overall laptop market has been contracting for two consecutive years, but TrendForce forecasts OLED laptop shipments will grow nearly 40% year-over-year in 2026, followed by another increase of more than 40% in 2027, with brands increasingly prioritizing OLED models in their product roadmaps.

exclusive panel supplier for the new MacBook Pro. The company has designated Phase 1 of its G8.6 A6 production line at its Asan campus in South Korea as a dedicated facility for Apple, and the MacBook Pro is the first product to enter mass production on Samsung Display's G8.6 fine metal mask (FMM) OLED line. The display's tandem OLED architecture and 254 PPI pixel density impose exceptionally demanding production requirements, particularly in material costs and manufacturing yields, notes TrendForce.


Meanwhile, rival panel makers are conducting qualification programs, but TrendForce believes the cost of meeting Apple's specifications and Samsung Display's established position present considerable barriers to entry. LG Display, BOE, and TCL CSOT are instead said to be directing their efforts toward the supply chain for the OLED MacBook Air, which isn't expected to debut until at least 2028.

title: Apple Executive Comments on New iPad Mini Lacking 120Hz Display
content:
While the new iPad mini has an OLED display, the device does not support ProMotion, meaning the display's refresh rate is limited to 60Hz instead of 120Hz.


ProMotion support would have allowed for the iPad mini's refresh rate to automatically adjust from 10Hz to 120Hz depending on the content being displayed, but evidently Apple has kept the feature exclusive to the iPad Pro among iPad models for now.

interview with YouTuber and podcaster Christopher Lawley, Apple's vice president of hardware design David Pakula commented on the new iPad mini lacking 120Hz support, noting that its OLED display still has significantly faster pixel response times compared to the previous model with an LCD, resulting in reduced motion blur. 



"Display experience is about more than just a single spec," said Pakula. "One of the things that's really cool about OLED is it actually has this really fast pixel response time. So it's like more than an order of magnitude faster than the pixel response time for an LCD display. And what that does is it makes everything really smooth. Motion blur is significantly reduced compared to LCD. When you pair that with the other things that I mentioned, the contrast, the brightness, and the color, this is just a killer display."

Apple says the new iPad mini can achieve a maximum brightness of 600 nits for standard content, up from 500 nits for the previous model, and up to 1,200 nits for HDR content. OLED technology allows for higher contrast and more vivid colors, as there is no backlight and individual pixels turn off completely to display true black. 

Apple's tech specs indicate the new iPad mini has a 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio. The display still has 326 pixels per inch and P3 wide color support.

title: Apple Lowers App Store Fees in Taiwan Starting October 31
content:
Apple is lowering the commission that it collects in Taiwan to 26 percent, down from 30 percent. Apple plans to drop the rate for in-app purchase and paid app transactions on the iOS and iPadOS Taiwan storefront starting on October 31.


The commission update comes after Apple held discussions with the Taiwan Fair Trade Commission (TFTC). In a statement to MacRumors, Apple said the fee reduction reflects its ongoing commitment to developers. 
We're making updates to the Taiwan storefront of the App Store following constructive discussions with the Taiwan Fair Trade Commission. These changes reflect our ongoing commitment to providing developers with a thriving marketplace and ensuring the App Store remains the safest, most trusted platform for users. We will continue to equip developers with the tools, resources, and support they need to build, grow, and scale successful businesses on the App Store.
Apple previously adopted the 26 percent commission rate in Japan and the European Union. Apple also negotiated a 25 percent commission in China after discussions with China's State Administration for Market Regulation.

title: Best Mac 2026: Every Apple Mac and MacBook compared
content:
Macworld





Choosing the best Mac in 2026 means finding the right combination of performance, features and price for the way you work. Whether you’re buying your first Mac, replacing an older computer or looking for more power, this guide will help you understand your options and choose with confidence.
Do you need a laptop to carry around or a desktop for a permanent workspace? Which processor will handle your apps, how much memory and storage should you buy, and which connections do you need? We explain what these differences mean in practice, helping you identify the features worth paying for.
We also help you work out the total cost. Memory and storage upgrades can significantly increase the price, while some models require a separate display and accessories. Our configuration advice and retailer price comparisons will help you balance your needs against your budget and decide where to spend – or save.
Below, you’ll find our recommendations followed by detailed explanations of every current Mac family, including their strengths, limitations and upgrade options. Together, these will help you narrow your shortlist and choose the right Mac for your work, home or studies. For a closer look at Apple’s laptops, see our MacBook comparison.
Best Mac 2026: Mac & MacBook Buyers Guide
The MacBook Air is our top Mac for most people in 2026, offering an excellent balance of performance, portability, battery life, and value. For tighter budgets, the MacBook Neo starts at $699/£699 and is Apple’s most affordable laptop.
For demanding creative and professional work, choose the MacBook Pro. The touchscreen MacBook Pro adds the flexibility to interact directly with the display alongside the keyboard and trackpad.
If you don’t need portability, the Mac mini, starting at $899/£899, offers good value if you already own a display and accessories. The iMac combines the computer and display in an all-in-one design that’s ideal for the home, while the Mac Studio provides greater power for intensive creative work and AI development.

What is it? The 13-inch MacBook Air is Apple’s thin and light laptop for everyday use, offering more performance and features than the cheaper MacBook Neo.
What’s new? Apple introduced the M5 MacBook Air in March 2026, featuring the M5 chip with its faster CPU and GPU. The base configuration now starts with 512GB of storage (double the previous model), along with faster SSD speeds, more memory bandwidth, and support for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.
Who’s it for? It’s perfect for students and everyday users who want a lightweight laptop that’s easy to carry, and powerful enough for working, studying, browsing, and doing light creative work. If you want a larger screen there is a 15-inch MacBook Air, which we discuss below. 
How much does the 13-inch MacBook Air cost? The entry-level 13-inch M5 MacBook Air costs from $1,299/£1,299, that’s up $200/£200 from the launch price of $1,099/£1,099. You can create build-to-order models with more memory (up to 32GB) or storage (up to 4TB).
What are the specifications? The standard specs for the M5 MacBook Air offer an improvement compared to the previous generation. The MacBook Air now ships with 512GB SSD as standard. 
Apple M5, 10-core CPU, 8-core GPU, 16GB memory, 512GB SSD, two Thunderbolt 4 ports: $1,299/£1,299.
Apple M5, 10-core CPU, 10-core GPU, 16GB memory, 512GB SSD, two Thunderbolt 4 ports: $1,399/£1,399.
Additional options: Up to 32GB memory, 4TB storage.
What are display specifications? 
While referred to as 13-inch, when measured diagonally the screen is 13.6-inches.
The 13.6-inch Liquid Retina on the M5 MacBook Air display has a native resolution of 2,560×1,664 and 500 nits brightness.
The MacBook Air M5 can support two external displays.
How do I connect stuff? The M5 MacBook Air models supports Thunderbolt 4, which means that they can support a dual monitor set up. If you want to connect USB-A devices, you need either a USB-C to USB-A adapter, like Apple’s $19 / £19 one, or a USB-C hub that has USB-A ports. In the U.K. and Europe Apple has stopped including a Power Adapter in the box, so you will need to buy one separately. See our round-up of the best USB-C hubs and adapters.
The 2026 MacBook Air offers Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) for connecting to a network. It also provides built-in Bluetooth (6) for wirelessly connecting a mouse or other peripherals. If you want to connect to an ethernet network, you need an adapter.
How fast is it? In our tests the M5 saw consistent gains over the M4 in the previous generation, as you can see in our Mac processor benchmarks. In some benchmarks the M5 even beats the M1 Ultra. If you are upgrading from an old Mac – especially if it is one with an Intel chip – you will see a huge difference.

Read more about the Mac mini’s storage changes. If you need more memory, Thunderbolt 5, or stronger multicore CPU and GPU performance for demanding workloads, look at the M5 Pro Mac mini instead. 1.
What’s best, MacBook Air or MacBook Pro?
We explore this question in detail in our MacBook Air vs MacBook Pro comparison. The MacBook Air is the best choice for most people, offering enough performance for everyday work, studying and many creative tasks. The MacBook Pro is worth considering if you need sustained performance for demanding workloads, more ports or a more advanced display.
The entry-level MacBook Air costs $1,299/£1,299, although you can often spend less by shopping around – we regularly round up the best MacBook Air deals. If you want more screen space without paying for professional-level performance, the 15-inch MacBook Air is considerably cheaper than a 14-inch MacBook Pro.
Within the MacBook Pro range, the standard 14-inch M6 model provides a middle ground between the Air and the more expensive M5 Pro and M5 Max configurations. Its fan helps maintain performance during longer processing tasks, while its Liquid Retina XDR display, HDMI port and SDXC card slot add flexibility.
The M5 Pro and M5 Max models suit more demanding professional workloads, offering more CPU and GPU cores, higher memory capacities and Thunderbolt 5. M5 Pro is a strong option for software development, photography and video editing. Consider M5 Max if your work benefits from its additional graphics power, media engines or higher memory ceiling; spending more won’t necessarily make everyday tasks noticeably faster.
You can also choose a MacBook Pro with a PROLED XDR touchscreen. Available in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes, these models add an OLED display, touch controls alongside the keyboard and trackpad, Dynamic Island, and a thinner, lighter design. Starting at $2,899/£2,899 for the 14-inch model and $3,399/£3,399 for the 16-inch, they cost $400/£400 more than equivalent non-touch M5 Pro models. They use the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chip families, so the main reasons to pay extra are the display, portability and touch input.
Choosing between a 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro comes down to workspace, portability, battery life and price. The larger model gives you more room for editing timelines, coding and multitasking, while the 14-inch is easier to carry. Both sizes offer powerful Pro and Max configurations. For external monitors, current M5 Pro models support up to three displays and M5 Max models support up to four, depending on resolution and refresh rate.
For a tighter budget, the MacBook Neo lowers the starting price of a Mac laptop to $699/£699. It’s worth comparing its compromises with a discounted previous-generation MacBook Air before deciding.





2.
Should I upgrade from my Intel Mac?
Yes. It’s time! We are now more than six years into Apple’s transition from Intel processors to its own silicon that includes CPU, GPU, and unified memory. The transition began with the introduction of the M1 in November 2020. Since June 2023 every Mac Apple sells uses Apple’s own chips rather than Intel processors.
If you’ve yet to upgrade your Intel Mac to one powered by Apple’s silicon what are you waiting for? If you are concerned that a must-have app doesn’t run on an M-series Mac, consider finding a new app because the performance gains are tremendous.
Another good reason to replace an Intel Mac is that Apple’s support for these models is winding down. macOS Golden Gate, released in September 2026, is the first major version of macOS to support no Intel Macs. Intel Macs compatible with older versions of macOS may continue receiving security updates for a limited period, but they are now outside Apple’s current feature-release cycle. Apple does not guarantee how long those updates will continue, and machines limited to macOS Sequoia are likely to lose support sooner than those capable of running macOS Tahoe. Read: How long does Apple support Macs.





3.
Where can I get the best price for a new Mac?
Apple rarely offers direct price cuts on new hardware, but resellers frequently do. Getting the best price on a new Mac requires knowing where to look and when to buy: 
Top U.S. Retailers:
Amazon: Often has the lowest prices, especially during events like Prime Day. For example, during the July 2026 Prime Day event, a 14-inch M5 MacBook Pro was available for $1,749, a $450 discount. Even outside of events, Amazon frequently undercuts Apple’s MSRP.
Best Buy: A reliable source for discounts and trade-in offers. In late 2025, Best Buy offered a massive $1,150 off an M2 Ultra Mac Studio.
B&H Photo: A well-regarded authorized reseller that often has competitive pricing on Macs.
Walmart: Known for exclusive deals on older models, like the M1 MacBook Air, which has been sold brand-new for just $599.
Top U.K. Retailers:
Amazon UK: Similar to the U.S., Amazon UK is a primary source for discounts.
KRCS: An Apple Premium Reseller that frequently offers good deals.
John Lewis & Currys: Reliable high-street retailers that often have competitive prices and good customer service.
If you’re looking for a great offer, visit our Best Apple Deals page which is regularly updated.





4.
What specs do I really need for my Mac?
Chip: The specs you need depend on what you plan to do with your Mac. For web browsing, email, office apps and light photo editing, a standard M-series chip is more than sufficient. The M6 is available in the Mac mini, iMac and standard 14-inch MacBook Pro, while the MacBook Air uses M5. The budget MacBook Neo uses an A18 Pro chip. A newer generation number doesn’t automatically make a chip better for every workload: compare its CPU, GPU, memory and capabilities with what your apps actually need. 
If you regularly work with complex spreadsheets, large Photoshop files, audio projects, video editing or more demanding games, look at a Pro chip. The M5 Pro Mac mini, for example, offers up to an 18-core CPU and 20-core GPU and up to 64GB unified memory.
A Max chip is worth considering for demanding graphics, complex 3D work, high-resolution video production or projects that need more memory than a Pro configuration supports. Many developers, photographers and video editors will be well served by a Pro chip. The M5 Max offers an 18-core CPU, up to a 40-core GPU and up to 128GB unified memory, depending on configuration. 
The M5 Ultra, with up to a 36-core CPU, 80-core GPU and 512GB unified memory, is aimed at the most extreme workloads, including VFX, scientific computing and running very large AI models locally.
GPU: One of the biggest differences between Apple’s chips is GPU performance. Standard M-series chips are easily sufficient for everyday graphics, casual gaming and light creative work. Pro chips add considerably more GPU power for video editing, graphics work, 3D applications and gaming. Max chips are designed for professional graphics, high-resolution video and demanding 3D workflows, while Ultra provides Apple’s highest GPU performance. The M5 Max offers up to 40 GPU cores, while the M5 Ultra doubles that to 80 GPU cores. Both also have Neural Accelerators built into every GPU core to speed up AI workloads.
RAM: Apple calls RAM Unified Memory. The MacBook Neo is limited to 8GB, which is probably the biggest drawback of that machine. Most Macs start with at least 16GB, which is plenty for everyday use, although we recommend choosing more if your budget allows because the memory cannot be upgraded later. 24GB or 32GB is a good choice for heavier multitasking, photo editing, podcasting, moderate video production and gaming. Developers and professional creative users may benefit from 48GB, 64GB or more. The new M5 Pro Mac mini can be configured with up to 64GB, M5 Max Mac Studio with up to 128GB, and M5 Ultra Mac Studio with an enormous 512GB.
Storage: Even with iCloud and external drives available, it can seem like you can never have enough storage inside your Mac. 256GB may be sufficient for basic web and office use, but it can fill up quickly. We recommend 512GB for most people who want to keep a Mac for several years, particularly if you store photos, games or media locally. For regular video or audio production, 1TB or more is preferable. Professional users may need several terabytes. The M5 Pro Mac mini offers up to 8TB, while the M5 Ultra Mac Studio and touchscreen M5 Max MacBook Pro offer up to 16TB. Maximum capacity varies by model and chip, so check the configuration you’re considering. Choose enough internal storage when ordering rather than relying on a later internal upgrade. An external SSD can add capacity for media libraries, project files and archives, often at a lower cost than Apple’s internal storage upgrades.
Display: Consider screen quality and workspace alongside processing power. The MacBook Air’s display is suitable for everyday work and many creative tasks, while MacBook Pro models add XDR brightness and ProMotion refresh rates. The PROLED XDR models also offer OLED, Adobe RGB support and touchscreen input in a lighter design. Choose them if those features will benefit how you work; they use the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chip families as the non-touch versions.
For more information to help you decide which Mac to buy see our Mac processor comparison where we compare Apple silicon and Intel. We also offer advice about how much storage, RAM, and cores in How much MacBook RAM, SSD, GPU, and CPU do you really need.





5.
When were the Macs last updated?
In March 2026, Apple introduced the M5 MacBook Air, the 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Pro and M5 Max, and the new MacBook Neo. All went on sale on March 11.
On August 25, 2026, Apple announced the Mac mini with M6 and M5 Pro, and the Mac Studio with M5 Max and M5 Ultra. Both ranges went on sale on September 22.
On October 27, 2026, Apple announced the M6 iMac and standard 14-inch M6 MacBook Pro. The following day, it introduced the 14-inch and 16-inch touchscreen MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR displays and M5 Pro or M5 Max chips. In-store availability for these October models begins November 6.
Apple discontinued the Mac Pro in March 2026. The Mac Studio is now its highest-end desktop Mac.





Why you can trust Macworld’s advice
Macworld has been covering everything Apple related since our first issue which arrived alongside the original Mac in 1984. Nobody knows Apple better, except probably Apple, but the difference is that we are completely impartial. We are made up of a team of experts with decades of experiences with Macs and other Apple products, and between us we have reviewed every Apple product meaning we are uniquely positioned to provide buying advice.
Price increases June 2026
In June 2026, Apple increased prices significantly across several product lines including Macs, iPads, the Apple TV 4K, and HomePod models, citing an unprecedented rise in component costs. 
The company stated it had “never seen a component price increase this much, this quickly” and that it had shielded customers from these increases for as long as possible before finally raising prices. 
For Macs, prices increased from $100/£100 to $500/£500 depending on the model.

title: Old 'Popcorn Time' App Left Hundreds of Thousands of Macs at Risk
content:
If you installed Popcorn Time on a Mac years ago, part of the app may still be running, and it may have left your Mac open to attack.


Security firm Eye Research has detailed how Time4Popcorn – an unofficial version of the once-popular movie streaming app – left behind a small update checker that scanned for updates every time the Mac started, even for people who hadn't opened the app in years. The checker basically trusted whatever it downloaded, and gave it full permission to change anything on the Mac.

What's worse is that Time4Popcorn's developers long abandoned the project, so the website addresses the helper contacted were expiring. That meant anyone who took over one of the addresses could use it to install harmful software on affected machines. Fortunately, Eye Research says it found no evidence that criminals had done so.

Is It Worth Upgrading?

For most existing M5 Pro and M5 Max ‌MacBook Pro‌ owners, there is little reason to upgrade. Both versions use the same chips, so equivalent configurations should deliver essentially the same processing performance. Neither the maximum memory capacity nor battery life has increased.

16TB option accommodates projects that exceed the older model's storage ceiling. These are essentially reasons to upgrade for a particular workflow, rather than for better everyday performance.

The touchscreen is a welcome addition for some users, but it is highly unlikely to justify replacing a recent ‌MacBook Pro‌ by itself. The upgrade case is stronger for users coming from an M1-, M2-, or M3-generation ‌MacBook Pro‌, particularly when their current machine is struggling with demanding work or has insufficient memory or storage. The existing configuration and the work it needs to perform matter more than its age alone.

Its ‌OLED‌ panel is the main reason to pay more, while touch input, reduced weight, and improved speakers make the overall package more appealing. Users who need its advanced display and production capabilities have the clearest reason to choose it.

title: The best touchscreen MacBook is already on your desk
content:
Macworld





Apple rarely arrives first to the party, but it tends to deliver an innovative twist when it eventually catches up to its rivals. AirPods, Face ID, Apple Watch, even the iPhone Duo weren’t the first of their kind, but they stood out for their leaps in design and functionality. However, as the launch of Apple’s first touchscreen MacBook Pro just proved, that’s not always the case.
Commercial touchscreen laptops have been around for almost two decades. Despite that, standard models have remained the default for valid reasons, most notably due to their perfect ergonomics. Instead of perfecting the formula as it usually does, Apple distracted fans with a recycled favorite—slapping on a glowing logo that had been retired a decade ago.
What makes the touchscreen MacBook especially baffling is how unnecessary it is. Apple already figured out the touchscreen setup back in 2019, and it’s been hiding in plain sight all these years.
Sidecar attachment
Sidecar was released as part of macOS Catalina in 2019. Billed as a way to expand your workspace, it essentially lets you use an iPad as an external wireless display for your Mac. Once it’s connected via AirPlay, you can drag Mac windows to your iPad’s screen and interact with them as you would on your Mac. Most controls were previously limited to Apple Pencil or mouse and keyboard input, but with macOS 27, you can use your fingers, too. There’s even a handy Sidebar on the ‌iPad‌ for common controls, like bringing up the on-screen keyboard or returning to the iPad’s Home screen, along with the Touch Bar that was previously included with certain MacBook models.

				
					

				
			
Sidecar turns your iPad into a wireless external display for your MacBook.

Apple




Unhinged design
Steve Jobs famously opposed touchscreen laptops because “after an extended period of time, your arm wants to fall off.” When reading early rumors about the touchscreen MacBook, I had expected—or at least hoped—Apple would do something different by incorporating an innovative hinge mechanism. A convertible form factor would have allowed users to interact with the touchscreen horizontally and easily switch back to the traditional laptop mode whenever needed. Alas, that did not come to fruition.
I acknowledge that we shouldn’t take everything Steve ever said as gospel because technology evolves, but many of his remarks still hold true today. The main issue with touchscreen laptops has never been weight or thickness, as some Apple execs recently suggested. At no point while using my MacBook does it feel natural for me to extend my arm and touch its display, and most people would probably relate. The new MacBook Pro is no different, and a sturdier hinge and lighter chassis don’t resolve the actual problem.
Sidecar is a whole different story, however. My iPad is untethered from the MacBook’s keyboard, letting me flexibly touch its screen horizontally or otherwise. This allows me to utilize touch input on macOS when the need arises without straining my arm. It’s precisely the kind of innovation Apple is generally praised for, and we’ve already had it for years.
Out of touch
The MacBook Pro with a PROLED XDR Display caters to professional creatives by letting them interact with macOS apps using their fingers. Yet, curiously, the machine is seemingly incompatible with many of these professional creatives’ go-to accessory: the Apple Pencil. This bars power users from taking advantage of precise interactions, pressure sensitivity, tilt detection, and all the other perks they cannot achieve with their fingers.
Meanwhile, Sidecar on the iPad supports Apple Pencil input—not to mention that iPadOS can run many desktop-class creative suites natively. So, whether you’re Sidecar-ing or using the iPad independently, you get to unlock advanced creation controls and workflows that surpass what you can do with the new MacBook Pro.
Beyond functionality, using an Apple Pencil minimizes fingerprints on your display, and creators know all too well how relevant that is. I’m far from being a professional photographer, but I’m constantly wiping down my 13-inch iPad Pro M4 before editing pictures because color correction and healing blemishes on the pixel level require that kind of clarity. Without Apple Pencil support, the new MacBook Pro’s display is going to get all smudgy as you attempt to get work done.

				
					

				
			
You don’t need a touchscreen MacBook if you already have an iPad.

Apple




Mac Duo
Another advantage for using Sidecar as a separate wireless monitor for your Mac is having two sets of app windows open on each screen simultaneously to work on more complex tasks. Touch Bar enthusiasts will also be delighted to learn that the discontinued MacBook feature lives on through Sidecar.
Non-MacBook Pro users, like those with a Mac mini/Studio, MacBook Air, or iMac, will especially appreciate being able to utilize the touchscreen without spending almost $3,000 on a new laptop—all thanks to Sidecar. In fact, it might be wiser to buy a Mac mini and an iPad Pro than a touchscreen MacBook Pro. Let’s break it down.
An M5 Pro Mac mini ($1,699) combined with an iPad Pro M5 ($1,199) costs $2,898—a dollar less than the touchscreen MacBook Pro (M5 Pro)’s starting price. With this package, you’d be getting one of the most advanced tandem OLED panels on the market and two desktop-grade processors instead of one, not to mention Apple Pencil support and far greater versatility.

				
					

				
			
Sidecar gives you the versatility you won’t get in a touchscreen MacBook.

Foundry




Pick a side
I’ve long depended on Sidecar with my MacBook Air, and—unlike the touchscreen MacBook Pro—it remains a prominent example of Apple’s classic “It just works” philosophy. The built-in feature requires absolutely no setup, cables, or technical literacy. Your Mac magically pairs to your nearby iPad and lets you mirror or extend the display wirelessly. That’s the epitome of touchscreen support on a laptop, even surpassing the highly advanced convertibles in terms of practicality and overall user experience.
Ultimately, if touchscreen laptops were truly essential, they would’ve evolved meaningfully throughout the past years, and Apple wouldn’t have waited this long to release one. Professionals have been using standard laptops for decades just fine, and add-ons like Wacom graphics tablets continue to thrive among digital artists due to their precision and horizontal designs.
Steve Jobs once said that people don’t know what they want until you show it to them. Apple already showed us the right way to do touch on a Mac with Sidecar, and it shouldn’t have caved to market pressure to build the wrong one.

title: Apple Releasing HomePod Mini 2 Tomorrow With These New Features
content:
Following more than two weeks of pre-orders, the HomePod mini 2 will begin arriving to customers and launch in stores this Friday, October 30.


Siri AI will be one of the HomePod mini 2's key upgrades, but the feature will not be available at launch. Apple said Siri AI support on the speaker will arrive in a future software update, but it did not say when the update will be released.

Siri AI is the more intelligent and personalized version of Siri powered by Apple Intelligence that launched on the iPhone 15 Pro and newer in September.

HomePod mini 2 is powered by the Apple Watch Series 10's S10 chip, up from the Apple Watch Series 5's S5 chip in the original HomePod mini. Apple said the S10 chip enables "advanced computational audio," but it did not explicitly confirm if the HomePod mini 2 has improved sound quality compared to the original model.

The speaker now supports faster Wi-Fi 6E, up from Wi-Fi 4.

new fourth-generation Apple TV 4K can connect to four HomePod mini 2 or full-sized HomePod 2 speakers in front and rear pairs, allowing for surround sound. Many home theater enthusiasts will prefer to use a proper 5.1 surround sound system with a center speaker and a subwoofer, but this basic all-Apple system at least exists now, and Apple says the front two HomePods virtualize the center channel to some extent.


You can mix and match HomePod mini 2 and full-sized HomePod 2 speakers for surround sound, so long as the front and rear pairs match. For example, you could have two full-sized HomePod 2 speakers as the front pair and use two HomePod mini 2 speakers as the rear pair. A related Whole Room Audio feature is offered for parties.

on Macs with Wi-Fi 6E and later. The full-sized HomePod 2 also supports this capability now — make sure to install the latest HomePod software version 27.2 via Apple's Home app.

There are three Siri microphones in the HomePod mini 2, down from four in the previous model.

Sound Glow feature, the top of the HomePod mini 2 glows and pulses in sync with the music playing. You do not need the new model, though, as a software update extended this feature to the original HomePod mini and the full-sized HomePod 2.

title: Up to 350,000 Macs exposed by a forgotten Popcorn Time updater
content:
An abandoned Popcorn Time updater left up to 350,000 Macs vulnerable to remote takeover, giving potential attackers a way to execute malicious code with full system privileges.

Popcorn Time
Security researchers at Eye Research detailed the discovery in an October 22, 2026, research report about Operation IXIM. The vulnerability affected Time4Popcorn, an abandoned fork of the popular BitTorrent streaming application that continued circulating under the Popcorn Time name after the original project shut down in 2014.
Some users had stopped using Popcorn Time, but its updater kept running. Eye Research discovered attackers could hijack it to install malware and intervened between November 2025 and March 2026.

title: Next Apple event: Expected dates and what Apple could launch next
content:
Macworld





Apple’s “Pro and Tell” media experience, took place in Los Angeles on October 28, 2026. The company announced its first touchscreen MacBook Pro, officially called MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display, featuring tandem OLED, Dynamic Island and a thinner, lighter design.
It completed a week of announcements that included the iPad mini with A20 Pro on October 26 and the standard 14-inch M6 MacBook Pro and M6 iMac on October 27. Preorders are open, with availability beginning November 6.
Apple has not announced a date for its next event. Attention now turns to possible spring 2027 launches, although new products could arrive through press releases or another media experience rather than a keynote.
Apple’s annual event calendar typically includes WWDC in June and the iPhone event in September, with additional launches sometimes taking place in spring and October. Dates are rarely confirmed far in advance, but past schedules and reliable reporting offer clues for anyone planning to buy a new Apple device. Here’s everything we know about Apple’s next event, including the date, start time, expected announcements and what could follow.


When is Apple’s next event?
Spring 2027 is the next likely window for an Apple event, although the company has not confirmed a date.
Over the past decade, Apple has held spring events and media experiences on several dates:
March 4, 2026
May 7, 2024
March 8, 2022
April 20, 2021
March 25, 2019
March 27, 2018
Apple can also announce products without holding an event. In 2025, it introduced the iPhone 16e in February, followed in March by the seventh-generation iPad Air, 11th-generation iPad, MacBook Air and Mac Studio.
That makes spring 2027 a plausible window for further launches, whether Apple holds an event, invites the media to a hands-on experience or announces products through press releases.


						

							


What will Apple announce at its next event?
The iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e are expected to arrive in spring 2027, making them likely candidates for Apple’s next announcements. The iPhone Air 2 could also appear, although rumors suggest Apple may combine it with the iPhone 18 rather than release a separate model.
Other possibilities include a 12th-generation iPad with support for Apple Intelligence, expected in 2027, and an updated full-size HomePod. 


						

							


Will Apple livestream the next event?
Apple doesn’t livestream its media experiences, but for events like WWDC and the iPhone launch in September, it livestreams a keynote presentation.


						

							




Apple event calendar 2027: What will Apple launch?


TimescaleEvent themeDatesProducts

Spring iPhone eventTBCExpected: iPhone 18, iPhone 18e
JuneWWDC7 June (predicted)Expected: To reveal plans for: iOS, macOS and other software
SeptemberiPhone eventTBCExpected: New iPhones, new Apple Watch

 



				
					

				
			
Calendars at the ready.

Foundry





 FAQ 


1.
How far in advance does Apple announce an event?
Apple usually announces its events around one to two weeks before they take place, although the timing varies. The October 13, 2026 Experience was announced just five days in advance. Apple also sometimes chooses to announce products via press release without holding an event. 





2.
How long do Apple Events usually last?
Apple keynotes usually last between one and two hours and feature the CEO alongside various other Apple executives.
WWDC and the September event tend to be longer keynotes; the spring and late-fall events can be slightly shorter. 
For example, the September 2024 keynote event was 1 hour 38 minutes.





3.
What time do Apple events normally start in U.S., U.K. and other global time zones?
Apple’s keynote events tend to start at 10 am PT or 1 pm ET. That translates to the following times in the countries where most of our readers live:
U.S.: 10 am PDT, 11 am MDT, 12 pm CDT, 1 pm EDT
Canada: as above, plus 2 pm ADT
U.K.: 6 pm
Europe: 7 pm CEST, 8 pm EEST
India: 10:30 pm IST
Australia: next day — 1 am AWST, 2:30 am ACST, 3 am AEST
New Zealand: next day — 5 am NZST
The timings are generally the same for all Apple Keynotes, but can be slightly different if Apple holds the event during the period of a couple of weeks when the clocks have changed in the U.S. but not elsewhere.
Sometimes Apple holds events at different times, for example, in October 2023 the event was held in late afternoon in San Francisco, which meant it was midnight in the U.K. The event on October 13, 2026 started at 9 am in New York, 2 pm in the U.K.
If Apple doesn’t hold an event and instead just issues a press release, that usually happens around 8 am PT, 11 am ET and 4 pm U.K. time.





4.
How often does Apple hold events?
There can be as many as four Apple events in a year:  
Spring Event
WWDC in June
iPhone Event in September
Late Fall Event in October
This event calendar is by no means set in stone, though, with the spring and October events being less regular. Some years, Apple doesn’t hold a spring event at all. In 2025 Apple only held two events, preferring instead to announce new products via press release.





5.
Will there be a live stream at the next Apple Event?
Apple usually livestreams the iPhone announcement in September and the WWDC keynote in June.





6.
Does Apple ever announce products without an event? 
Apple frequently announces products without a keynote event, often opting for press releases or multi-day announcement windows. In recent years, the company has increasingly reserved its large-scale media events for major flagship launches, such as the primary iPhone lineup in September, while using press releases for iterative updates or “chip bumps” that may not warrant a full hour-long presentation.





7.
How to watch an Apple event
Apple events are typically broadcast across several digital platforms, allowing viewers to tune in from almost any device. While the company previously restricted access to its own hardware or the Safari browser, these barriers have been removed in recent years.
You can access live Apple presentations through the following official channels:
YouTube: This is often considered the easiest way to watch. Apple streams its keynotes live on its official YouTube channel, which can be accessed via any web browser or the YouTube app on smartphones, tablets, and smart TVs.
Apple.com: The company hosts a dedicated “Events” page on its official website. 
Apple TV App: The stream is available within the Apple TV app on iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple TV hardware. Keynotes are usually listed in the app’s lineup a day or two before the event begins.
Apple Podcasts: Apple also showcases its events through the Podcasts app on Apple devices, where you can watch the video presentation.
We usually run a Live Blog which will provide minute-by-minute text updates and analysis as products are announced.
Following the end of the event, detailed breakdowns will also be available on the Macworld Podcast, which can be found on Spotify, Soundcloud, and Apple Podcasts. 








Will Apple hold a spring event in 2027? 

				
					

				
			John Ternus: Apple’s new CEO.
Michael Simon / Foundry




Apple’s spring events have become increasingly unpredictable. The company has not held a traditional spring event since May 2024, although it did invite members of the media, including Macworld, to a “Special Apple Experience” in 2026. 
Rather than a keynote presentation, the March 4, 2026 gathering was a hands-on showcase that followed three days of product announcements, including the MacBook Neo, iPhone 17e, and M5 MacBook Air.
Will Apple take a similar approach to spring product launches in 2027? It’s certainly possible. The format appeared to work well, allowing each product announcement to receive its own media coverage rather than competing for attention during a single event. 
Apple is expected to release three iPhone models in spring 2027 – or it could be two new iPhones, with the Air and iPhone 18 merging.
iPhone 18 
iPhone 18e
iPhone Air 2
Apple may also update the MacBook Air with an M6 processor and the MacBook Neo in spring 2027.


						

							


When is WWDC 2027?

				
					

				
			
Foundry




When is the WWDC keynote?
In 2026 the WWDC keynote was on Monday June 8. In 2025 it started on Monday June 9. We expect WWDC will start on Monday 7 June in 2027. 
WWDC generally runs from the Monday to Friday in the second week of June. 
What Apple could launch at WWDC
WWDC is Apple’s big developer event at which it reveals plans for the operating systems that run on Apple hardware.
In June 2027 we expect Apple to unveil details of iOS 28, iPadOS 28, macOS 28, updates to watchOS, tvOS, HomePod software, and an update to Apple’s visionOS.
Apple sometimes announces new hardware at WWDC, usually the high-end models targeted at power users, so we could see new Macs.
Following the keynote on Monday, developer events and sessions will run throughout the week. You can read more about WWDC date, times and everything you need to know in a separate article.


						

							




Apple event calendar 2026: What did Apple launch in 2026?
Apple held five events and hands-on media experiences in 2026, alongside several launches via press release:
March 4: Hands-on experiences followed announcements of the iPhone 17e, M4 iPad Air, M5 Pro/Max MacBook Pro, M5 MacBook Air and MacBook Neo.
June 8: WWDC introduced Apple’s upcoming operating systems, including iOS 27 and macOS 27 Golden Gate.
August: Apple announced new Mac mini and Mac Studio models via press release.
September 9: Apple unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, iPhone Duo, Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, and AirPods 5.
October 13: “Welcome Home” introduced HomeView, HomePod mini 2, a fourth-generation Apple TV 4K and the Apple Home Collection of smart-home accessories.
October 28: “Pro and Tell” showcased the touchscreen MacBook Pro, plus the M6 MacBook Pro, M6 iMac and iPad mini announced earlier that week.

What did Apple launch at past events?
In 2025 Apple only held two events. The first was its Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC) on June 9, at which it introduced the new features coming in the next version of its operating systems, and the second was the huge September 9 Apple Event where it launched new Apple Watches, new AirPods Pro and the new iPhones for 2025.
Apple doesn’t have to hold an event to launch new products though. Prior to WWDC, Apple launched a new iPhone 16e via press release on February 19, a new iPad and iPad Air via press release on March 4, and a new MacBook Air and Mac Studio on March 5. 
Apple then went on to launch a new M5 MacBook Pro and M5 iPad Pro in October. No event was held to mark these launches.
In 2024, Apple held three events: one on Tuesday, May 7, at which it launched new iPads; a keynote to kick off WWDC on June 10; and an event on September 9 at which Apple unveiled the new iPhone 16, Apple Watch Series 10 and the AirPods 4. In October 2024 there was no event, but Apple did announce new products (iMac, Mac mini and MacBook Pro) via press release.
In 2023 there were three events: WWDC in June, an iPhone event in September, and Apple’s second fall event on October 30 (or after midnight on October 31 if you weren’t in the U.S.).
In 2022 Apple held three events: a spring event on March 8, WWDC on June 6, and the iPhone 14 launch on September 7. In other years Apple has held four events though.

title: New Apple products coming in 2027: What’s next?
content:
Macworld





It’s been a huge year for Apple, with new products arriving throughout 2026. March brought the MacBook Neo and iPhone 17e, followed by the new Mac mini and Mac Studio in August.
September delivered another wave of launches at Apple’s “Surprise and Shine” event, including the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max, iPhone Duo, Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, and AirPods 5.
Apple turned its attention to the smart home at its “Welcome Home” gathering on October 13, unveiling HomeView, HomePod mini 2, a new Apple TV 4K and the Apple Home Collection. More announcements followed: a new iPad mini on October 26, then a 14-inch MacBook Pro and iMac with M6 chips on October 27.
Apple completed that week’s announcements on October 28 with the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display – its first touchscreen Mac. The new 14-inch and 16-inch models feature tandem OLED displays, Dynamic Island and thinner, lighter designs. Preorders are open, with availability beginning November 6.
What will Apple announce next?
With the touchscreen MacBook Pro now announced, attention turns to Apple’s 2027 lineup. Reports point to a spring launch for the standard iPhone 18, iPhone 18e and potentially an updated iPhone Air, alongside a new entry-level iPad with Apple Intelligence support. 
Apple’s roadmap: At a glance
As of September 1, 2026, Apple’s roadmap has come under the direction of CEO John Ternus. Former CEO Tim Cook has moved into the executive chairman role. The shift from an operations-focused leader to one with deep hardware engineering roots could signal a more product-driven approach – and a renewed emphasis on standout hardware. 


ProductExpected timingKey rumors

iPhone 18/iPhone Air 2Spring 2027 rumorediPhone 18 could merge with iPhone Air
iPhone 18eSpring 2027 rumoredPossible Dynamic Island
iPadSpring 2027 rumoredApple Intelligence support
20th-anniversary iPhoneFall 2027 rumoredMajor redesign; possible iPhone 20 branding
Camera-equipped AirPods2027 rumoredCameras for AI features rather than conventional photography

Apple Smart GlassesUnknownCameras, audio, Siri/Visual Intelligence

Apple products announced in 2026
Here is what Apple has already announced in 2026:
MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display: Bringing OLED touchscreens, Dynamic Island and a thinner, lighter design to 14-inch and 16-inch M5 Pro/Max models. 
MacBook Pro M6: A standard, non-touchscreen MacBook Pro; M6 performance upgrade, Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.
iMac M6: M6 and connectivity upgrades; existing 24-inch design and seven colors retained.
iPad mini: 8.5-inch OLED display, thinner and lighter design, water and dust resistance, landscape Center Stage camera.
HomeView: A new smart-home display with a 7-inch touchscreen, available in tabletop and wall-mounted versions.
HomePod mini 2: An updated speaker with an S10 chip, new colors and Siri AI coming through a future software update.
Apple TV 4K: A fourth-generation model with an A19 chip and an updated Siri Remote.
Apple Home Collection: Cameras, doorbells, locks and thermostats developed with accessory partners.
iPhone Duo: Apple’s first foldable iPhone: iPhone Duo Guide.
iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max: A20 Pro chip, upgraded vapor-chamber cooling, camera improvements: iPhone 18 Pro & Max Guide.
Apple Watch Series 12 & Ultra 4: Faster chips, Apple’s latest health-sensing features: Apple Watch Series 12 & Ultra 4.
AirPods 5: Stronger open-ear Active Noise Cancellation and longer battery life: AirPods 5.
Mac mini M6 and M5 Pro: Faster storage, upgraded connectivity, and a strong focus on AI performance: New Mac mini 2026 guide.
Mac Studio M5 Max and M5 Ultra: Faster AI and graphics performance, increased memory bandwidth: New Mac Studio 2026 guide.
AirPods Max 2: Improved audio and the H2 chip. Find out more here: AirPods Max 2 guide.
MacBook Neo: Apple’s brand new, low-cost Mac laptop. Find out more here: MacBook Neo guide.
MacBook Air M5: Now with the M5 chip. Read about the 2026 MacBook Air here: MacBook Air M5 guide.
MacBook Pro M5 Pro & M5 Max: A significant upgrade over the M4 series. Read: MacBook Pro M5 Pro & Max guide.
Studio Display: Finally gets Thunderbolt 5 and a better webcam. 
Studio Display XDR: With mini-LED technology and ProMotion up to 120Hz.
iPhone 17e: The new, entry-level, iPhone replaces the iPhone 16e. Read more here: iPhone 17e guide.
iPad Air M4: The iPad Air now has an M4 chip. Read more here: iPad Air M4 guide.
AirTag 2: Four years on Apple updated the AirTag, read our review here: AirTag 2nd gen review.
And… RIP Mac Pro: Apple has confirmed that it is discontinuing its tower workstation.  
Read on to find out what new products to expect at Apple’s next event and in 2027 and beyond.


						

							


Every New Apple Product Launching in 2027 and beyond
In the sections below we’ve split the upcoming new products into categories including Mac, iPad, iPhone, Apple Watch, Home, AirPods, and some new product categories.


						

							







What new iPhones are coming in 2027?
Reports point to a split iPhone launch schedule in 2027, with the iPhone 18, iPhone 18e and potentially an updated iPhone Air arriving in spring. A major redesign could follow in the fall to mark the iPhone’s 20th anniversary. There is a lot of speculation about whether Apple will use the iPhone 19 or iPhone 20 name.

				
					

				
			There are new iPhones coming.
Foundry




iPhone 18 & iPhone 18e
Spring 2027 launch expected
The iPhone 18 and 18e are rumored to arrive together in the spring of 2027. Both could gain A20 chips and more RAM. The iPhone 18 is expected to retain dual rear cameras and gain a 24MP selfie camera; the 18e may keep one rear camera and a 60Hz display. Read about the iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e rumors. 
iPhone Air 2
The iPhone Air could also be getting an update. But there are rumors that it will actually merge with the iPhone 18. See our iPhone Air 2 rumors.
iPhone 19 or 20 – 20th anniversary iPhone 
Apple’s 20th-anniversary iPhone could feature curved glass, ultra-thin bezels and two larger display sizes. Under-display Face ID could reduce the camera cutout. See our iPhone 19 or 20 rumors – because one thing nobody is sure about is whether Apple will skip 19 like it skipped 9 with the arrival of the iPhone X. 
Should you buy now or wait? 
If you need an iPhone now, compare current models with discounted older stock and refurbished alternatives. If your existing phone still meets your needs and you’re considering a standard or lower-cost model, waiting for the rumored spring 2027 launches may give you more choice. See our guide to When is the best time to buy an iPhone.


						

							


Which new iPads are coming in 2027?
Don’t expect major redesigns for the iPads. Instead, Apple is likely to focus on faster chips and other internal upgrades. That said, the iPad is due an update – particularly as it lacks support for Apple Intelligence. Here’s what we expect Apple to announce:

iPad (12th generation)

title: How macOS Adapts Its Controls for Touch on the New MacBook Pro
content:
Apple announced a new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display on Wednesday. It's Apple's first Mac with a screen that supports touch, and demonstrations Apple gave to the media show how macOS reshapes its controls for finger input. Menu bar items expand under a fingertip, window controls get bigger, and the Dynamic Island pulls down into a floating widget, amongst other changes.


Back in 2016, then-senior VP of marketing Phil Schiller (now Apple Fellow) argued that putting touch on a Mac display would mean "totally redesigning the menu bar for fingers" – something he said would clash with pointer devices. Apple's modern solution, however, is more subtle. The menu bar looks the same, but when you move a finger over a menu item, it expands to let you make a selection with more precision.

The same idea applies elsewhere in the macOS interface. For example, the traffic-light buttons that control window size and position also get bigger when you touch them, after which you make your selection with a tap. You can also swipe up from the bottom of the screen to reveal a hidden Dock.

A Pull-Down Dynamic Island


Elsewhere, the new MacBook Pro replaces the notch with a Dynamic Island where Spotlight, Live Activities, and Siri AI live. You can pull down on the Dynamic Island to open an expanded version that floats on the screen like a widget, giving you access to Siri responses and Spotlight search.

Apple says macOS automatically translates touch into clicks, so many existing apps will work with touch right away – no developer updates required. Possible interactions include swiping to scroll a webpage, pinching to zoom in on a photo, dragging and dropping slides between presentations, and double-tapping a window to fill the screen.

pull-to-refresh gestures in apps like Safari, Mail, and Calendar, while code in macOS 27.2 added touch-specific gesture recognition in Safari, Notes, Photos, and Quick Look.

Precision Work in Pro Apps


It appears that touch isn't just for casual swipes either. Pro application features have also been updated to work with fingers, such as color grading in DaVinci Resolve and tweaking soundtracks in Logic Pro.

title: Russia orders Apple to surrender users' messages on demand
content:
Apple and Microsoft have been added to a Russian state surveillance registry, requiring them to hand over users' text, video and audio messages without a legal process, and by request.


Moscow at night (Credit: Evgenit/Pixabay)
Multiple firms and apps are already on this same list, including WhatsApp and Telegram, so it's not clear why it has taken until now for Apple to be added. It's a continuation of the country's moves to control users' messages, though, as it follows Russia's blocking of FaceTime in 2025.
According to Bloomberg, Apple and Microsoft were added to this registry of "organizers of information dissemination" on October 2, 2026. The registry is operated by the country's state media watchdog, Roskomnadzor, which previously forced Apple to remove VPN apps from the App Store.

The monitor might be the second-most important part of your Mac’s setup after the Mac, of course–you can’t use any desktop computer without one and even the 16-inch screen on the MacBook Pro feels cramped if you are having a particularly productive morning. Spread your work out by plugging in multiple monitors to your Mac and extending your desktop over a wider space.
Because you’ll spend a lot of time looking at the display, you’ll want to invest wisely. Not only will you want a monitor that provides a pleasing experience, but the quality of the images on the screen can also affect your work.
However, picking a new monitor can be daunting. Not only are there many manufacturers to choose from, but there are also lots of sizes, resolutions, and features to consider—and when we say lots, we mean lots. We’re here to help guide you while you shop, and we have some tips on what to look for in a monitor plus advice on how many monitors each Mac can handle.
Best Mac monitors 2026
These are the best desktop Mac monitors we have tested. We round up the best portable displays for Mac separately if you want to take a larger display out on the road or easily store one out of sight when you’re not using it.
We’ve included Apple’s Pro Display XDR and the Apple Studio Display, not because they are necessarily the best choice, but for comparative purposes.

It offers a great range of adjustment: -5 to 20 degrees of tilt, swivels 15 degrees left or right, and 115 mm of height. The display can also pivot 90 degrees to Portrait mode, a far greater range of motion than the Studio Display. 
The MA270U/P can connect to a Mac through HDMI or USB-C. The USB-C connection offers 90 watts of power so it can charge your MacBook at the same time. If you want to use the display as a connection hub, you need to connect to the Mac via USB-C. Its built-in spare USB-C port offers 15W of power output and the USB-A 7.5W. There are two HDMI ports so you can connect to another device for multitasking.
The one thing that’s immediately noticeable with the MA270U/P is its impressive image quality. Colors are full of life and the detail is excellent. One standout aspect of the image quality is how sharp text appears. This is great for production and design work, but it can even make it more enjoyable to read and write.
It offers image quality that could satisfy users in a production environment–that’s one way of saying that its quality is better than what general users usually get. You might be able to find a 27-inch 4K display that’s a little cheaper, but it won’t look this good.–Roman Loyola
